top5.title: Google unveils two new TPU chips and increases pressure on Nvidia
top5.description: Google introduced two new versions of its eighth-generation TPUs, which are used to train and run Gemini. They are expected to ship in 2027, while TPU sales could exceed $135 billion in 2028.
top5.why: Google’s new TPUs could materially intensify competition with Nvidia and reshape the economics and supply chain of AI infrastructure when they ship.

top5.title: Anthropic unveils its Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models
top5.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, touting them as 30% faster and 20% cheaper than the 5.1 generation. The models underwent new safety and alignment testing.
top5.why: Anthropic’s faster, cheaper Claude models could accelerate enterprise AI adoption while increasing competitive and pricing pressure across the frontier-model market.

top5.title: AI data center boom prompts political backlash in the United States
top5.description: Voters have opposed the growth of AI-dedicated data centers, and new restrictions could slow construction, raise costs, and alter capacity distribution. The affected regions, regulations, and business risks remain worth monitoring.
top5.why: Political opposition to AI data centers threatens to slow capacity expansion, raise infrastructure costs and change where future computing power is built.

top5.title: OpenAI creates a kill switch for its research models
top5.description: OpenAI developed Control Room, a system capable of cutting off a research AI model’s access to its outputs. It tracks training, evaluations and data processing, but a cached authorization can delay shutdown by 35 seconds.
top5.why: OpenAI’s Control Room represents a significant step toward operational governance of powerful research models, although its 35-second shutdown delay exposes residual safety risk.

top5.title: Claude reveals more than 100 vulnerabilities in UK government projects
top5.description: Using Claude Opus and Sonnet, a researcher found vulnerabilities in roughly two-thirds of 349 public projects belonging to 33 UK organizations. One vulnerability provided read and write access to SharePoint and OneDrive spaces containing HR files.
top5.why: Claude’s discovery of vulnerabilities across roughly two-thirds of tested UK public-sector projects highlights the urgent cyber risk created by AI-assisted vulnerability research.
